 Novira Cymru Leagues Games to Watch: 20-21 November
 Posted on 19 November, 2026 19 November, 2026 Posted in Novira Cymru North , Novira Cymru Premier , Novira Cymru South Share Share Close Modal Copy Link Link copied to your clipboard 
 Following last weekend’s  FAW Welsh Cup  action, the  Novira Cymru Leagues  return in full this weekend, with a top-of-the-table clash among the standout fixtures. Here are the key games to watch. 
 Novira Cymru Premier – Penybont vs Haverfordwest County (Friday, 7:45pm ) 
 Haverfordwest County play their first Novira Cymru Premier fixture without former manager Tony Pennock when they travel to face Penybont at the Dragonbet Stadium on Friday. 
 Pennock, who guided Haverfordwest to their joint-record finish in the Novira Cymru Premier and two European qualifications, brought an end to his four-and-a-half year managerial reign on Tuesday with the club sat 11th in the table and 13 points adrift of the top six. The Bluebirds have enjoyed a spell of resurgence recently though, winning four out of their last five matches – a run which includes a 3-1 victory over Ammanford in the FAW Welsh Cup third round last weekend. 
 Pennock’s shock departure was announced on Tuesday evening 
 Penybont head into Friday’s fixture in bright form themselves, winning 10 out of their last 11 matches. Rhys Griffiths’ side maintained their unbeaten streak on home turf this season with a 2-0 win over Caernarfon Town last time out in the Novira Cymru Premier – a result which keeps them nine points behind leaders The New Saints with a game in hand. Bont were also victorious in FAW Welsh Cup action last weekend as they beat second tier outfit Cardiff Draconians 6-0 thanks to braces from Chris Venables, Billy Borge and Ioan Phillips. Tyler Walker has been clinical in front of goal as well recently, scoring in each of his last four games. 
 Bont emerged as 3-0 winners in August’s reverse Phase One fixture against Haverfordwest, taking their unbeaten streak against their fellow South Walians to 11 matches.

 Watch Live on Cymru Football TV 
 Novira Cymru Premier – Airbus UK Broughton vs Colwyn Bay (Friday, 7:45pm) 
 Two teams with high ambitions for top six spots meet as Airbus UK Broughton host Colwyn Bay at the Hollingsworth Group Stadium on Friday.
 Airbus made it five consecutive top-flight wins for the first time in their entire history following their hard-fought 3-2 victory at Holywell Town a fortnight ago – a game which also saw current Novira Cymru Premier top scorer George Peers net his 17th goal of the season. During their five-match winning streak, the Wingmakers have remarkably scored a minimum of three goals on each occasion and they would leapfrog Colwyn Bay into fourth-place with another victory on Friday. 
 Airbus have won their last three matches by the same 3-2 scoreline 
 Bay clinched a 2-1 victory over Trefelin at the beginning of November to make it back-to-back away wins and strengthen their place inside the top six. Stoppage time goals from Adam Davies and Ethan Roberts were required for Michael Wilde’s side last weekend as they edged past Novira Cymru South side Aberystwyth Town 2-0 in the FAW Welsh Cup. The Seagulls are now looking to extend their unbeaten run in all competitions to seven matches – something they have never managed to do while in the Novira Cymru Premier. 
 Davies was the difference in August’s reverse Phase One fixture, scoring the only goal in a 1-0 win for Bay as Airbus were punished for failing to convert their glorious chances during that match.

 Watch Live on Cymru Football TV 
 Novira Cymru North – Brickfield Rangers vs Newtown (Saturday, 2pm) 
 The current Novira Cymru North top two face off as leaders Brickfield Rangers host second-place Newtown at Clywedog Park on Saturday. 
 Brickfield have dropped points in their last two home games, but a 3-1 victory at Buckley Town at the beginning of November – Brickfield’s fourth consecutive away win in the league – helped maintain their four-point lead at the top of the table. Saturday’s exciting clash is the perfect opportunity for Gareth Wilson’s side to bounce back from their 1-0 defeat to Novira Cymru South outfit Caerau Ely in the FAW Welsh Cup last weekend and strengthen their position at the summit. 
 Newtown will be eager to take all three points back to mid-Wales on Saturday as victory would take the Robins just one point behind Brickfield with a game in hand. Josh Astley scored in 2-0 wins over Buckley and Ruthin Town to help Newtown maintain pressure at the top of the table before the in-form attacker bagged two more goals in a 3-1 victory over Caerphilly Athletic in the FAW Welsh Cup last weekend. Jay Owen’s side are still unbeaten away from home this season, winning five and drawing once from their six league matches on the road. 
 Hanoch Boakye has contributed to a goal in each of his last five in all competitions 
 Jamie Hyne found the net three times across Newtown’s 4-1 and 2-0 wins over Brickfield in the Novira Cymru North last season. 
 Novira Cymru South – Pontardawe Town vs Baglan Dragons ( Saturday, 2pm ) 
 Pontardawe Town aim to make it six matches unbeaten in the Novira Cymru South when they host Baglan Dragons in a local derby at Parc Ynysderw on Saturday. 
 Pontardawe were left stunned when they lost to fourth tier Llangennech in the FAW Welsh Cup last month, but there was an impressive and quick response as Ponty triumphed 2-1 against Carmarthen Town for their third straight home win. Steve Berry’s side would have been disappointed to let a two-goal lead slip in a 3-3 draw with bottom side Llanelli Town last time out, but that was still a result which took them up to 11th in the table and two points clear of the relegation zone. 
 Jesse Meacock has nine goal contributions in his last five in the Novira Cymru South 
 Baglan will be making the short trip to Pontardawe in high spirits after they nearly pulled off a memorable FAW Welsh Cup shock in a penalty shootout loss to top-flight Barry Town United last weekend. Goals from Tom Randall and Toby Jones secured a 2-1 win for Baglan in their last league outing, which lifted the Dragons up to sixth-place, meaning they have every reason to be confident of claiming another three points on Saturday. 
 This will be the first competitive meeting between Pontardawe and Baglan since the 2023/24 Novira Cymru South season, where both teams enjoyed a 2-1 victory over each other.
